strings.name: Reed Hastings
strings.role: Netflix cofounder, former CEO and former chairman
strings.summary: Reed Hastings cofounded Netflix with Marc Randolph and helped move it from DVDs by mail to streaming subscriptions, original programs and global distribution, reshaping film and television consumption. His record also includes the failed Qwikster split and customer backlash. He left the CEO role in 2023 and the board in 2026, while supporting education and joining Anthropic's board to engage with technology and society.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Cofounds Netflix and advances online streaming, changing audiovisual-content distribution, subscription consumption and industry competition.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Mathematics bachelor's, Bowdoin College; computer-science master's, Stanford University
strings.highlights.h1.title: From DVDs to streaming
strings.highlights.h1.text: With the team, he developed online disc rentals into a streaming platform, changing viewing through subscriptions and global distribution.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Education and technology governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: He supports education philanthropy and Bowdoin's AI-and-humanity research; Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust appointed him to its board in 2025.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Leaving Netflix's board
strings.timeline.t1.text: His term ended after the annual meeting and Jay Hoag became chairman; he had already become nonexecutive chairman in 2025.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Stepping down as co-CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: He became executive chairman as Greg Peters joined Ted Sarandos in leading the company; the change was publicly announced on January 19.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Major international expansion
strings.timeline.t3.text: At CES he announced entry into over 130 additional countries, greatly expanding reach while still excluding markets including China.
strings.timeline.t4.title: House of Cards premieres
strings.timeline.t4.text: Netflix released all 13 first-season episodes, a milestone for its original programming and full-season viewing; creative and production teams made the series.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Qwikster split abandoned
strings.timeline.t5.text: Following backlash over pricing and plans to separate DVDs, Netflix cancelled the branding split. Hastings had already apologized for mishandled communication.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Instant PC viewing introduced
strings.timeline.t6.text: Netflix announced phased internet viewing for members while retaining DVDs by mail, beginning its streaming transition.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Netflix Nasdaq listing
strings.timeline.t7.text: Shares began trading as NFLX, raising capital for business development.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Cofounding Netflix
strings.timeline.t8.text: With Marc Randolph he established the company, which launched online DVD rentals in 1998.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Founding Pure Software
strings.timeline.t9.text: He started a software-tools business that went public and merged before Rational acquired it in 1997.
strings.timeline.t10.title: Stanford master's degree
strings.timeline.t10.text: He earned his computer-science master's after a 1983 Bowdoin mathematics degree and Peace Corps service teaching mathematics in Swaziland.
